metric: ld: function identification and comparison with /bin/ld (nonsegmented, E711, stripped)
metric_def: instruction comparison with tools/ldcheck.py (cc -O object of the draft against the original code range); own code 0x0042..0x2c4c; crt0 0x0000..0x0042 is generated (mkcrt0.sh)
schema: functions: name -> file (our source), ours (range of the draft), orig (start in /bin/ld), pairing (open|confirmed), level (open|exact|findings), status (open|done|findings:<classes>); findings: list of findings with id, status, functions, orig, ours, summary, done, decide; findings_pending: items without a D class; manual_classes: hand notes per function (basis read|open, note); d_classes: differences of the old compiler (D1..)

binary_facts.magic: E711 (nonsegmented, I and D separate: data addresses from 0, bss after the data)
binary_facts.strings: SCCS: crt0.s 3.2 (generated), ld.c 1.18, copyname.c 1.3, printname.c 1.5, symbols.c 1.8
binary_facts.libc: libc part 0x2c4c..0x49bc (shipped members and oldlibc versions, tools/ld.spec)

main.note: exact (2026-10-29): the option scan with the goto structure of sld main; the whole ld.c compiles to the same 724 bytes and instructions (addresses masked, frame offsets equal). The draft alone (ldcheck) shows jr/jp widths only, because the calr calls to in-file functions are sized by the whole file (HANDOFF_ld.md).

parse_args.note: exact (2026-10-29): the argument pass with the switch on the option letters (table at data 0xf8, b/t fall into e/o/u/v, N, l with the '-' written before the letter). Checked in the whole-file compile of ld.c (174 bytes, same instructions, frame kept); the draft alone would differ in calr sizes.

f26ac.note: exact (2026-10-29): the frame difference was one unused 2-byte local (spare), as in HOWTO step 7. The earlier char-parameter theory was wrong.

f26ca.note: exact (2026-10-29): the frame difference was one unused 2-byte local (spare), as in HOWTO step 7. The earlier char-parameter theory was wrong.

f21f2.note: exact (2026-10-29, fifth attempt): for loop, the equal case is the main path (if (*t == *s++) { if (*t++) continue; return(1); } return(0)); parameter list (t, s). The earlier D1/D15 reading was the pointer copy and the branch sense, both resolved by the form.

f226e.note: exact (2026-10-29, fifth attempt): char c (second argument, r7) and register pointer p (r6 -> r14); struct buf { int _x; int _cnt; char *_ptr; } (the displacements of the original: cnt at 2, ptr at 4). The struct member _x is a name guess; the layout is what matters.

f1b0a.note: exact (2026-10-29, fifth attempt): parameter list (q, p, n), register pointer r and counter i (declared in this order), and two unused int locals (spare1, spare2). The parameter order is the same as f1f22 and f1b0a stands for the rule; the register order (r14 then r13) as in f1f22.

f1f22.note: exact (2026-10-29, fourth and fifth attempt): parameter list (end, x) and three unused int locals (spare). The parameter order is the one of f1b0a: the first declared parameter takes the last argument register. Frame 18 bytes as the original.

f221e.note: exact (2026-10-29, first attempt): put of an int into the buffer (high byte, then low byte), parameter order (x, p); x is the first declared parameter (last argument register r7), p the register pointer. Uses the shared struct buf.

f050c.note: exact (2026-10-29, second attempt): append entry to the table tab (22-byte records, index ntab): t0 = x, t1 = v44a6, t2 = v0070 (data), t3 = y, t4..t10 = v66d0, v66d2, v66d4, v66c2, v66c6, v66cc, v66ce. One unused int local. No caller in the table (its callers are through the table or unknown). Globals: ntab (bss 0abe), tab (0ac0), the v-names are guesses; v0070 is in the data (step 5b).

mget.note: exact (2026-10-29): sld mget structure with the text stream. Global `struct stream text` at bss 1030 (ptr 1030, bno 1032, nibuf 1034, size 1036, pno 1038; ptr first, as in get). Two unused int locals of the original frame are kept as spare1..spare3 (frame 16). Statement order as in the source: i = n; i >>= 1; r = p. Former name f1a9a. Renamed also: f1c6c -> get (sld get(sp)), f1b38 -> dseek (sld dseek(sp, v, n)).

dseek.note: findings (ld.c): sld dseek(sp, v, n) of ld. Six attempts: the frame and the register assignment (obj r14, cur r13) are right; the long compare of bno with hi is in rr4 in the original and in rr2 here (register choice, D3-like); two tests of the page pointer are loaded through r2 in the original (test @r2) and direct here (test @r13). The bno temporary (attempt 4) made it worse. Draft (attempt 3): /mnt/share/cvs/P8000/tmp/tmp/d5/f1b38_v3.c. Accepted into ld.c as a finding.

get.note: findings (ld.c): getw-like read of a word from a stream (sld struct stream layout, Plexus-like field order). The body is equal except (1) the parameter home slot: the original spills p (ld @r15,r7), the draft does not (D4); (2) the arguments of the refill call f1b38(p, -1, (long)(bno + 1) << 8): the original passes -1 in r3, the draft in r6, because the callee f1b38 (same file, defined before) fixes the argument registers and the draft is compiled alone. Check in the whole-file compile. Draft: /mnt/share/cvs/P8000/tmp/tmp/d5/f1c6c_v3.c.

flush_buffer.note: exact (2026-10-29, fourth attempt): struct buf { int _fd; int _cnt; char *_ptr; char _buf[256]; }; the parameter is a register variable (r14), n a register variable (r13), one unused int local. Note: the struct is a guess for the layout (fd, cnt, ptr, buffer of 256 bytes), the code only needs the offsets.

copy.note: findings (ld.c): copy of a file to the output buffer (lseek to 0, read 256 bytes, each byte put with f226e, close). Six+ attempts. Everything equal except the reload of the spilled parameter p before the fildes read: the original loads it into r7 (ld r7,p; ld r14,@r7), the draft into r2 (ld r2,p; ld r14,@r2). Also the frame needs two int spares before q (dec 12). Source behaviour of the original: the loop body runs while read returns more than 1 (cp r2,#1; jr gt), so a read that returns exactly 1 byte is not copied (quirk to record in KNOWLEDGE.md). Draft: d5/f1a12_try3.c. Accepted into ld.c as a finding.

sig_handler.note: exact (2026-10-29, first attempt): exit path: f2c02() if v669a, unlink("l.out"), chmod(v007a, ~umask(0) & 0x1ff) if no error, unlink(v007a) if v007c, _exit(v007c). Globals: v007a (char *, data 0x7a), v007c and v0080 (int, data 0x7c, 0x80), v669a and v66a4 (int, bss). The names are guesses from the use; step 5b checks the bss ones.

lookup_name.note: findings (symbols.c): sld lookup_name with ld names (cursym, nlflag, lnbuf, local, hshtab). Hash modulus 0x0923 in ld (sld 0x0ffa). Six attempts: the original keeps start (r11) and end (r10) in registers and slot, cur, rec in the frame or scratch; the draft has start and end in the frame and the loop test differs (cp r6,frame). Draft: d5/ln1.c. Accepted as finding.

next_entry.note: findings (symbols.c): sld next_entry with ld's 14-byte entries (exact step). Five attempts (d5/ne1..ne5). Register set differs (the original keeps only e in r12; p is in r1 without a spill). The bound test differs: the original compares p with two words of the table (symtab, symtab+nsym*14) in another order than sld's `p >= symtab && p < symtab + nsym`. Draft: d5/ne1.c. Accepted as finding.

put_sym.note: findings (symbols.c): sld put_sym without the struct copy: ld writes the symbol itself (mput(a, p, 14)) and has no nwsym count. Seven attempts (d5/ps1..ps7). Frame size 16 matches with two spares (ps4). Differences: swap_pair gets b from r6 in the original and from the frame here; the position of cnt (frame 7 in the original, 9 here). Draft: d5/ps4.c. Accepted as finding.

add16_checked.note: findings (ld.c): checked long sum of two unsigned parameters, error(1, p1) when the sum is 0x10000 or more, return of the low word. Three attempts: plain sum (int addition, wrong), signed long (addl needs the casts), casts (long). The instructions are equal except two reloads: the original loads p3 and p2 from the frame after the spill (ld r3,%0004(r15)) although they are in r7 and r6 (D3, redundant reloads). Draft: /mnt/share/cvs/P8000/tmp/tmp/d5/f089a_try3.c

pack_name.note: findings (copyname.c): sld pack_name with 14-byte steps (ld tables). Six attempts (d5/pn1..pn7). Frame, loops and calls equal; the padding loop test (cnt > 0) is inverted in the layout: the original has jr gt back to the loop and a separate jump to the zero test, the draft jr le over it. Draft: d5/pn3.c. Accepted as finding.

read_entry_hdr.note: owner decision: read_entry_hdr is in symbols.c (first function, address 0x249a), not printname.c. Exact before the move (34 instructions). symbols.c is now in address order (read_entry_hdr, lookup_name, slookup, pslookup, put_sym, put_all, warn_sym_redef, next_entry, f2bf6, f2bfc).

enter.note: findings (symbols.c): sld enter without the sseg store (ld symbols have no sseg; table size 0x0923). Five attempts (d5/en1..en5). Frame and calls equal with one spare int; the store *a = r is loaded through r2 in the original (ld r3,a; ld @r3,r2), the draft reloads r from r14. Draft: d5/en2.c.

getfile.note: findings (ld.c): sld getfile for ld (nonsegmented): library search with libname ("/lib/libxxxxxxxxxxx"), prefixes /usr and /z/bin, the strncpy count 0x168 - p, v66b4 selects .a or .8. The instruction count is equal (120). Differences: the original keeps three register variables (r12..r14), the draft two; the count of strncpy is computed as constant minus p (sub) and the last branch is inverted. The third prefix is not opened in the original (the final open of filname does it). reloc is a second stream whose address is not settled (pno at 0x1042, step 5b). Five attempts (d5/gf1..gf5, draft d5/gf4.c).

ensure_buf.note: findings (symbols.c): sld ensure_buf in its sld form (if (rlsize < n) with the zero test first, grow by f2b92 otherwise). 30 instructions, 29 equal: the original keeps a jump to the end after the grow call (jr), the draft falls through. The first form (rlsize >= n first) differed in the comparison copy and the branch sense. Draft: d5/eb9.c. Accepted as finding; the attempts in this round went beyond the limit of six (d5/eb7..eb10).

chk_ranlib.note: findings (symbols.c): sld chk_ranlib (ranlib entries of 12 bytes). Five attempts (d5/cr2..cr6, draft cr5). Loop, calls (pslookup, warn_sym_redef) and the frame size are equal with one spare int; the original stores q = p from a reload of the parameter (frame) and keeps a register variable (r14, not identified). Accepted as finding.

ranlib_scan.note: findings (ld.c): sld ranlib_scan with rltab (word at 0x6c00, a pointer) and rlcnt (0x6c02). Six attempts (d5/rs1..rs7, draft rs3). All calls and the frame (sv, t, end, i) are equal; the bound test rltab + i < end is computed through r3 in the draft and through r5 in the original (no form tried gave r5). Accepted as finding.

reg_sect_addr.note: findings (ld.c): sld reg_sect_addr for -t, -d, -b with the selector switch (t, d, b, end), tab42b4 (char[4], 0x702e), secorg (int[4], 0x7034), secspec (char, 0x702c). Six attempts (d5/rsa1..rsa6, draft rsa4). Equal code except the frame offset of fmt (6 in the original, 8 here) and the reduced frame. Accepted as finding.

init_entry.note: findings (ld.c): sld init_entry with the segment record of ld (struct fseg at p, flags x702f, x7030, x7031 as char, x66b8/x66ba for hy). Six attempts (d5/ie1..ie5, draft ie5.c). Equal except the store of hy: the original stores through r7 (hdr in a register), the draft reloads hdr from the frame. Accepted as finding.

readhdr.note: findings (ld.c): sld readhdr in its nonsegmented form (one argument: b is not used in ld). Six attempts (d5/rh_1..rh_6, draft rh_5). Equal in most of the code: header, segment records (16 bytes), counters c0..c2 from the atr bits of record 1, rounding for the nonsegmented case, flags x66b8/x66ba/x66b6. Open: the two error blocks (Bad format, Invalid segment attributes) are placed inline; the draft stores hdr fields in another order at the end. Accepted as finding; the draft has no separate store to fcdrel/fcbrel beyond the globals fcdrel (0x66d2) and fcbrel (0x66d4).

load2.note: findings (ld.c): sld load2 for ld (one long argument). Nine attempts (d5/l2_1..l2_9, draft l2_9, in ld.c). The loop over the symbols follows the original; the tail (dseek on text and reloc, half() offsets, the base increments of v6bf8, v6bfa, v6bfc) is now equal in the order of the calls; the remaining differences are the frame (2 bytes) and register choices in the loop (rr2 for the sums). Not yet exact.

load2td.note: findings (ld.c): sld load2td for ld (nonsegmented words). Nine attempts (d5/ltd1..ltd9, draft ltd9). Frame, the text and reloc reads, the swaps, the switch targets and the exit path are equal in the code; the remaining difference is the form of the first test and the text read of the loop (164 against 168 instructions). Accepted as finding.; word_put is f221e, swap is the libc swap (ld.h), v6bf6 is the open index base.

place_sec.note: findings (ld.c): ld place_sec (no parameters; areas[4] at 0x7004 with kind, tstart, tsize, tend; secorg, tab42b4). Four attempts (d5/ps_1..ps_4, draft ps_4): all branches, messages and stores are in, 233 against 242 instructions. The differences are the code of the kind and the zero-or-total ternaries (order of the immediate loads) and the overlap loop start. Accepted as finding.
